St. Cyril Lucaris

St. Cyril Lukaris · St. Kyrillos Loukaris · St. Cyril Loukaris · St. Cyril Lucar

Period
1572–1638
Region
Crete; Alexandria; Constantinople
Titles / vocation
Bishop · Hieromartyr
Commemoration
June 27

Introduction

A patriarch of Alexandria and Constantinople, commemorated as a hieromartyr. Alexandria’s canonization act appoints June 27 as his annual feast.

Read the published life [1]

BackgroundLife and notable eventsDeath and martyrdomRecognition and the confession controversyChronology
Death / martyrdom

Strangled on June 27, 1638, as recorded by Alexandria’s canonization act

Read circumstances and sources

Background

Born in 1572 in Herakleion, Crete, he became a monk at Agarathos and studied in Venice and Padua. The Patriarchate’s account describes work in Orthodox education and opposition to the Unia.

[2] Published Orthodox hagiography · Brief life history: birth, studies, and early service; preceding commemoration address

Life and notable events

He served as patriarch of Alexandria from 1601 to 1620 and then held the Constantinopolitan throne with repeated interruptions. His work included aid during an epidemic, support for printing, and an introduction to a vernacular New Testament translation.

[2] Published Orthodox hagiography · Brief life history: Alexandrian service, printing, and translation

Death and martyrdom

The patriarchal canonization act records that Janissaries strangled him on June 27, 1638, and threw his body into the sea. It recognizes him among the Church’s hierarchs and martyrs.

[1] Primary patriarchal and synodal act · Main biographical paragraph and synodal declaration

Recognition and the confession controversy

Alexandria’s synodal act is dated October 6, 2009, and establishes June 27 as his annual commemoration.

[1] Primary patriarchal and synodal act · Synodal declaration; closing date

The Patriarchate’s 2022 report records his inscription in Constantinople’s list of saints on January 11, 2022. Its 2025 report documents his June 27 commemoration in Cyprus.

[2] Published Orthodox hagiography · Paragraph on the Ecumenical Patriarchate’s January 11, 2022 decision · [3] Published Orthodox hagiography · June 27, 2025 liturgy and commemoration of Saint Cyril Loukaris

The Synod of Jerusalem in 1672 disputed the confession’s attribution to Cyril and rejected its doctrines. The timeline presents the authorship dispute and the contrasting historical accounts.

[4] Primary synodal text · Acts, introductory argument, printed pages 16–17: first and third propositions; subsequent doctrinal rejection
